title: Lisse sheaves on a stratum are closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions
statement:
Let $S$ be a topologically Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$.

1. If $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ is an exact sequence of $\Lambda_S$-modules with $F'$, $F''$
   lisse, then $F$ is lisse.
2. If $\phi\colon F\to G$ is a morphism of lisse $\Lambda_S$-modules, then $\ker\phi$ and
   $\coker\phi$ are lisse.

Consequently, for a Noetherian scheme $X$, $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under kernels,
cokernels and extensions in $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, is an abelian category, and
the inclusion is exact. A $\Lambda_X$-module is constructible iff it is lisse on each stratum
of a finite stratification (the scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$ is a field, so a finite constant
local model is a finite free module, [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]).

external.place: (2) The coefficient sheaves $E_S$, $\Qlb_S$ agree with those of Bhatt–Scholze (Lemma 6.8.2 of *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, together with [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]), and their lisse sheaves agree with ours.

(2) The coefficient sheaves $E_S$, $\Qlb_S$ agree with those of Bhatt–Scholze (Lemma 6.8.2 of *The pro-étale topology for schemes*, together with [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]), and their lisse sheaves agree with ours.

proof.text: *Local models over a field and extensions.* For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $\Lambda(*)$ is a field. A finitely presented scalar module $P$ has a finite basis, hence $P\cong\Lambda(*)^r$ and $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P\cong\Lambda_U^r$. Conversely take $P=\Lambda(*)^r$. Thus [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] gives exactly pro-étale local finite freeness. In the asserted short exact sequence, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies the inverse-image coefficient ring with the ring on the source. Its final assertion identifies module pullback canonically naturally with the lift of exact inverse image whose action is transported along that ring isomorphism. Thus restriction preserves the short exact sequence. Only the untwisted assertion is used; it imposes no invertibility hypothesis on $\ell$. Choose a common pro-étale cover trivializing $F'$ and $F''$. The underlying abelian-sheaf category is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], and its tensor is additive and preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], so the hypotheses of the module-cokernel statement hold. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], applied to the underlying abelian sheaves (module cokernels are computed there by [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels]), each of the finitely many basis sections of $F''$ lifts after a covering refinement; successive refinements lift them all. Sending the basis to these lifts defines a $\Lambda$-linear section $s$ of $F\to F''$. If $i:F'\to F$ and $p:F\to F''$ are the sequence maps, $(a,b)\mapsto i(a)+s(b)$ has inverse $f\mapsto(i^{-1}(f-s(p(f))),p(f))$, since $\ker p=\operatorname{im}i$. Therefore $F$ is locally a direct sum of two finite free modules. This proves extension closure, including rank zero.

source.place: Local models over a field; proof of (1)

proof.text: *Finite-field coefficient comparison and cokernels.* First take $\Lambda=E$. By [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring], $E_S=p_S^*C(-,E)$. The canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] identifies this ring with $V\mapsto C(|V|,E)$, exactly the rational coefficient ring in [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients] and Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.1. It preserves finite free local models, hence lisseness. This is the coefficient realization of Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1; it is not used as a local-freeness theorem. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization] to the finite diagram $F\xrightarrow{\phi}G$. On its connected qcqs étale cover $T\to S$, $\phi$ is $J_T(h)$ for an equivariant map $h:V\to W$ of finite-dimensional continuous $E$-representations. Put $I=h(V)$ and $Q=W/I$. Both are finite-dimensional. Their actions are continuous: choose a basis of $I$, extend it to a basis of $W$, and identify $Q$ with the complementary coordinates; the action matrices on $I$ and $Q$ are submatrices of the continuous matrix on $W$. The same basis calculation for $\ker h\subset V$ makes the induced action continuous. The exact sequences $0\to\ker h\to V\to I\to0$ and $0\to I\to W\to Q\to0$ therefore have exact images under $J_T$. Consequently the map $J_T(V)\to J_T(I)$ is epic, $J_T(I)\to J_T(W)$ is monic, and their composite is $J_T(h)$. The second sequence then says that $J_T(Q)$, with its specified quotient map from $J_T(W)$, is the ambient cokernel of $J_T(h)$. It is lisse by the comparison node. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) and its final assertion, module pullback is canonically naturally isomorphic to the exact lift of inverse image with action transported along the coefficient-ring comparison. It therefore preserves this ambient cokernel, which identifies it with the restriction of $\operatorname{coker}\phi$. This uses untwisted coefficients, so no invertibility of $\ell$ is required. Combining the étale covering with the pro-étale finite-free covers of $J_T(Q)$ proves that $\operatorname{coker}\phi$ is lisse on the original $S$. No new stratification is taken.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6) and Corollary 6.8.5, proof; coefficient comparison: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1

proof.text: *Algebraic-closure cokernels by the prescribed finite-coefficient passage.* Now let $\Lambda=\Qlb$. Fix the prime and algebraic closure already used for the coefficients. Use precisely the conventions in [det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-lisse]: finite coefficient fields are subfields of this fixed closure, $E_S=p_S^*\underline E$, and $\QbarS=p_S^*\underline{\Qlb}$ uses continuous sections with values in a finite subextension. Lisse means locally finite free on the small pro-étale site, including zero and varying ranks; scalar extension is the ordinary relative tensor product. These are the coefficient and locality conventions of the present item. A topologically Noetherian scheme $S$ is qcqs: every open, in particular $S$ and the intersection of two affine opens, is quasi-compact. Hence clause (1) of the descent node supplies lisse finite-field models of $F$ and $G$. Take the compositum $E_0$ of their fields inside the fixed closure; it is finite, since products of finite spanning sets span the compositum. Extend both models to $E_0$. Extending a local basis gives a local basis, so both models remain lisse. Tensor transitivity is the balanced map $r\otimes(s\otimes m)\mapsto rs\otimes m$, with inverse $r\otimes m\mapsto r\otimes(1\otimes m)$; thus their extensions to $\QbarS$ retain the specified isomorphisms with $F,G$. Transport $\phi$ through these isomorphisms. By clause (2), this actual morphism is the image of a representative $(E,\phi_E)$ of the Hom colimit for a finite $E\supseteq E_0$, where $\phi_E:F_E\to G_E$. The transition maps in that colimit are exactly scalar extension, so the same tensor identifications identify $(\phi_E)_{\Qlb}$ with $\phi$. The previous step shows $C_E=\operatorname{coker}\phi_E$ is lisse. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](2), extension of scalars is a left adjoint and preserves cokernels. Hence $\operatorname{coker}\phi\cong\QbarS\otimes_{E_S}C_E$, which is lisse since a finite local basis extends to a finite local basis. The coefficient ring is exactly the one in [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $\QbarS\cong\varinjlim_E E_S$. No identification with the ring of all functions continuous for the valuation topology on $\Qlb$, and no flatness or preservation-of-kernels assertion, enters this passage.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.4(3),(4),(6), finite-coefficient passage in Corollary 6.8.5; blueprint paragraph (2)

proof.text: *Kernels by finite-free duality.* On the chosen small pro-étale site, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applied to the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf Z$ makes the underlying abelian-sheaf category Grothendieck abelian: a sheaf of abelian groups has the unique $\mathbf Z$-action given by integer multiples, and every additive map respects it. Together with the closed symmetric monoidal tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], this verifies the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]. For either coefficient choice put $R=\Lambda_S$ and $P^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$ as in [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]. For lisse $F,G$, a local finite basis and its dual identify $F^\vee,G^\vee$ with finite free sheaves; these identifications also verify compatibility with restriction. The already proved cokernel assertions apply to $\phi^\vee:G^\vee\to F^\vee$, so $D=\operatorname{coker}\phi^\vee$ is lisse. Evaluation sends a section $v\in\ker\phi$ to the functional on $D$ induced by $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(v)$: it annihilates the transpose image because $\mu(\phi(v))=0$ for every local section $\mu$ of $G^\vee$. Conversely, for a local $R$-linear functional $a:D\to R$, take a finite basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $F$, its dual basis $e_1^*,\dots,e_n^*$, and set $v=\sum_i a([e_i^*])e_i$. Evaluating on $\sum_i b_i e_i^*$ gives $\sum_i b_i a([e_i^*])$, so this recovers the functional on $F^\vee$. Since it kills the image of $\phi^\vee$, every dual coordinate of $\phi(v)$ is zero and $v\in\ker\phi$. The two operations are inverse. They agree on overlaps and commute with restriction because their characterization by evaluation is independent of basis. Thus $\ker\phi\cong D^\vee$. A finite local dual basis of $D$ proves $D^\vee$ lisse, including rank zero. This establishes the kernel assertion for $E$ and $\Qlb$ without another local-freeness tool.

source.place: Paragraph (2); explicit elementary evaluation calculation after the cokernel assertion

proof.text: *Globalization and the abelian category.* Given constructible $F,G$ with a morphism $\phi:F\to G$, use [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1),(2) to find a finite stratification on which $F,G$ are lisse. For an extension, instead adapt the common stratification to the two constructible end terms $F',F''$; no lisseness of the middle term is assumed. Each locally closed stratum has Noetherian underlying space. By part (3) of that node, restriction is exact, so $(\ker\phi)|_S\cong\ker(\phi|_S)$, $(\operatorname{coker}\phi)|_S\cong\operatorname{coker}(\phi|_S)$ and the restricted extension sequence is exact. The preceding steps and [sk-def-sfb-constructible] therefore prove all three global closure assertions. They also prove the finite-stratification characterization in the statement, since local finite freeness is exactly the finite constant local model of step 1. The underlying abelian-sheaf category is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], and its tensor is additive and preserves finite colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Hence [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes the ambient module category abelian. The full constructible subcategory contains zero and finite direct sums (use $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$). Fullness gives the ambient kernel and cokernel their universal properties in this subcategory. Their iterates give its image and coimage, and the ambient coimage-to-image isomorphism and its inverse belong to the full subcategory. It is consequently abelian. Its kernels and cokernels are the ambient ones, so the inclusion is exact.
